sources: Novgorod's treaty charters with the princes of Tver (1264, 1266, 1270; Gramoty Velikogo Novgoroda i Pskova, nos. 1-3): Novgorod's volosts Volok, Torzhok, Bezhichi, Vologda, Zavoloch'e, Koloperem', Tre, Perm', Pechera, Yugra
J. Martin, Medieval Russia 980-1584 (2nd ed., 2007): Novgorod's northern tribute lands
Treaty of Nöteborg (1323) for the Karelian frontier as it had stood

Treaty of Almizra (1244) and the Castilian kingdom of Murcia: Villena, Almansa, Cieza, Mula and Moya were Castilian until the Aragonese war of 1296-1304 (Treaty of Torrellas 1304 gave Aragon only Alicante, Elche and Orihuela)

rules.note: Karelia between Lake Ladoga and the White Sea: Korela and the Karelians under Novgorod.
Tre, the Terek coast of the Kola peninsula, a Novgorodian tribute land (its northern Sami shared tribute with Norway).
Zavoloch'e, Pechora and Yugra: Novgorod's northern tribute lands up to the Urals (Perm' of the Vychegda has a realm of its own).
The kingdom of Murcia and Villena/Almansa were Castilian in 1291 (Treaty of Almizra 1244); Aragon took them only in 1296.
Moya, a town of the Castilian Serranía de Cuenca.
